title: Document the combined install and minimum engine version
summary: The client repository's README and CHANGELOG present the combined install command as the default documented install, describe the minimum supported engine version, the idempotent upgrade behaviour that never downgrades an equal or newer engine, the standalone engine install, and the startup message for a missing or too-old engine.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

checks.criterion: Reviewing the install part of the page, its first installation route is a single action that the text says installs the engine and the client together, and no other installation route appears before it.
Reviewing the install part of the page, nothing tells the reader they must first obtain or pre-install the engine in order to install the client.
Reviewing the install part of the page, the engine's standalone install is documented as its own separate path.
Reviewing the install part of the page, exactly one concrete minimum supported engine version is stated, together with the statement that an older engine is refused.

Reviewing the install part of the page, the repeat-install paragraph states that the engine is installed only when missing or strictly older and that an equal or newer installed engine is left untouched.
Reviewing the install part of the page, both the missing-engine message and the too-old-engine message are described and each is actionable.
Reviewing the page as a whole, it states that version and diagnostic output work without an engine while engine-backed commands fail with the actionable message.

Reviewing the page as a whole, the added prose contains no internal structure, step ordering, timing, duration, runtime bound or local environment detail, and no reference to a release that has not been published.
Reviewing the client's changelog, its entry for changes not yet released covers the four recorded user-visible changes.
Reviewing the whole change, every documented statement agrees with the behaviour of the shipped product, and no previously correct installation statement was made false.
